title: Anomalous magnetocaloric effects in the quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet BaCo$_2$V$_2$O$_8$
authors: Jiahao Yang, Chao Dong, Xinlong Shi, Zhuo Wang, Tiantian Li, Liusuo Wu, Junfeng Wang, Zhangzhen He, Liang Li, Yongkang Luo, Jianda Wu
abstract: We investigate the transverse-field thermodynamics of the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like antiferromagnet BaCo$_2$V$_2$O$_8$, whose tilted screw-chain geometry and anisotropic Landé $g$ tensor generate spatially modulated Zeeman couplings. Angle-resolved magnetocaloric-effect (MCE) measurements reveal a high-field temperature minimum near the transverse-field Ising critical field for $H\parallel[110]$ that persists and shifts only weakly upon field rotation. Tensor-network calculations show that the rotation-induced staggered transverse field rapidly lowers the Ising critical field and that the magnetic Grüneisen ratio changes sign near the high-field temperature minimum, consistent with experiment. Our results establish that a dominant MCE response can persist away from the Ising critical region, suggesting a route to magnetic cooling by tailoring anisotropic Zeeman-coupling configurations in quantum magnets.
summary: This paper investigates the magnetocaloric effect in the quasi-1D antiferromagnet BaCo2V2O8 by combining angle-resolved measurements with advanced tensor-network simulations. The research distinguishes between the field associated with the Ising critical point and a higher-field transverse response. It concludes that the MCE can be engineered by tailoring anisotropic Zeeman couplings, opening a route for magnetic cooling in quantum magnets.
main_problem: To determine whether the anomalous magnetocaloric effect (MCE) in the quasi-1D antiferromagnet BaCo2V2O8 is governed by the intrinsic Ising critical field or by transverse spin fluctuations when the applied magnetic field is rotated.
main_result: The dominant MCE response persists away from the intrinsic Ising critical region, suggesting that magnetic cooling can be achieved by engineering anisotropic Zeeman-coupling configurations in quantum magnets.
method: The study combines angle-resolved MCE measurements with tensor-network calculations (DMRG) on an effective XXZ spin chain model.
model_or_system: The system is the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like antiferromagnet BaCo2V2O8, modeled by an effective spin-1/2 XXZ chain Hamiltonian incorporating site-dependent Zeeman couplings due to the material's geometry and anisotropic g-tensor.
key_observables: Magnetocaloric effect (MCE), magnetic Grüneisen ratio ($\Gamma_H$), Ising critical field ($H_{	ext{thr1}}$), and high-field temperature minimum ($H_{	ext{mc2}}$).
important_parameters: Applied magnetic field up to 45 T, temperature range around 1.6 K, and field rotation angles ($\phi_1$).
main_assumptions: The system can be effectively described by an XXZ chain model, and DMRG methods are used to calculate ground state and finite-temperature properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and geometry for different field directions, showing experimental MCE dips and angle-dependent magnetization/susceptibility data.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model and experimental measurements, then using theoretical calculations (DMRG) to analyze the field dependence of various magnetic order parameters and thermodynamic quantities, culminating in a comparison between the theoretical and experimental findings regarding the MCE source.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed study of magnetic phase transitions and thermodynamic responses in a highly anisotropic quantum magnet, which is relevant for understanding magnetic field control over quantum ground states.
